$comment: Differences in what the first mode of scripts/check-hcp-drift.mjs does not compare (bounds, `pattern`, `format`, closed objects, merged unions), made on purpose, for its second mode (scripts/lib/hcp-drift-constraints.mjs). Each entry names the mapped object (scripts/lib/hcp-drift-map.json id), the member path as the check prints it and the kind (a bound keyword, `pattern`, `format`, `closed` or `union`); `detail`, when present, must match the finding's detail too; `object`, `path` and `detail` may use `*`. `patternEquivalences` lists pattern pairs, exact text, that accept the same strings. Every entry has a `reason` and a `ref` to the spec's field-mapping section or the editors' question (`Q<n>`). The first matching entry takes a finding, and an entry or equivalence that matches nothing is stale and fails the check. Never add an entry for a difference that is a mistake: fix the schema.

patternEquivalences.reason: The same language: the character classes list the same ranges in another order, and `\S` is `[^\s]`.
The same language: the hexadecimal character classes list the same ranges in another order.

entries.reason: A nominal bound equal to the request's 16 MiB `maxDocumentBytes`, which the framework's lints ask for (the schema-bounds lint of a request-side array, `checkFreeTextBounds` of a free-text string): it refuses nothing a document of acceptable size could carry, so the imported shapes keep only HCP's own constraints (question 42).

A nominal bound equal to the request's 16 MiB `maxDocumentBytes`, which the framework's lints ask for (the schema-bounds lint of a request-side array, `checkFreeTextBounds` of a free-text string): it refuses nothing a document of acceptable size could carry, so the imported shapes keep only HCP's own constraints (question 42).

An upper size bound HCP does not set: a Trust Tasks framework bound on what an hcp/* party writes (SPEC §7.3 item 19 and the schema-bounds lint), not an HCP requirement (the spec's "Where this payload is stricter than HCP's shapes" paragraph). Only a cap ours adds is allowed here; a cap HCP sets that ours lacks or loosens is reported.
entries.ref: specs/hcp/entries/query/0.1/spec.md#hcp-field-mapping (the "Where this payload is stricter than HCP's shapes" paragraph every carried spec has)
